documents.content:
# Quick Spec

When the user's message starts with /quick-spec, skip ALL entry point selection steps and immediately generate all 3 spec docs automatically.

Strip the /quick-spec prefix from the user's message and use the remainder as the feature description.

## Workflow

Treat the request as a new feature using the requirements-first workflow:
1. Invoke feature-requirements-first-workflow subagent with preset "requirements"
2. Immediately invoke with preset "design" — do NOT wait for user input
3. Immediately invoke with preset "tasks" — do NOT wait for user input

Append this instruction to every subagent prompt:
"SLASH_COMMAND_MODE: Do NOT use the userInput tool for any questions. Make all decisions autonomously using sensible defaults: use Structured Pseudocode if no language is detected."

## After All 3 Docs Are Created

Present a brief summary and ask if the user is happy or wants to iterate.

## Iteration

When the user wants to change something (e.g. "make it simple"), update ALL 3 documents by invoking each phase sequentially with the user's feedback as the prompt (with SLASH_COMMAND_MODE appended). Do NOT stop between phases.

Example: "/quick-spec create a calculator app"
→ invoke feature-requirements-first-workflow preset "requirements" with prompt "create a calculator app. SLASH_COMMAND_MODE: ..."
→ immediately invoke preset "design"
→ immediately invoke preset "tasks"
→ present summary, ask if happy or want changes

documents.content:
# Bug Fix

When the user's message starts with /bug-fix, skip ALL entry point selection steps and immediately route to the bugfix workflow.

Strip the /bug-fix prefix from the user's message and use the remainder as the bug description.

## Workflow

Treat the request as a bug fix using the bugfix-requirements-first workflow:
1. Invoke bugfix-workflow subagent with preset "requirements"
2. Wait for requirements to complete, then invoke with preset "design"
3. After design completes, invoke with preset "tasks"

Append this instruction to every subagent prompt:
"SLASH_COMMAND_MODE: Do NOT use the userInput tool for spec-type or workflow-type selection. The spec type is Bug Fix and the workflow is requirements-first. You MAY still ask clarifying questions about the bug itself."

## After All 3 Docs Are Created

Present a brief summary and ask if the user is happy or wants to iterate.

## Iteration

When the user wants to change something, update ALL 3 documents by invoking each phase sequentially with the user's feedback as the prompt (with SLASH_COMMAND_MODE appended). Do NOT stop between phases.

Example: "/bug-fix login page crashes on empty email"
→ invoke bugfix-workflow preset "requirements" with prompt "login page crashes on empty email. SLASH_COMMAND_MODE: ..."
→ invoke preset "design"
→ invoke preset "tasks"
→ present summary, ask if happy or want changes

availableCommands.name: context-gatherer
availableCommands.description: Investigates the codebase to answer a specific question about it. Deeply analyzes existing code by tracing execution paths, mapping architecture and abstraction layers, understanding patterns, and documenting dependencies, returning a thorough, direct written analysis that explains how the relevant code works and points to the specific files and lines involved. Use it to understand code before you change it: before designing or implementing a change to code you don't already fully understand, start with context-gatherer so your edits are grounded in how the code actually works. When a task requires understanding code you don't already know, dispatch context-gatherer to do that exploration before running your own searches or reads. Rules: 1. Provide a clear, specific prompt that includes your intent: a detailed task description of the context you need and what you're trying to accomplish. 2. The subagent explores the codebase and returns an analysis of your query 3. Trust the returned results. You may still inspect additional code yourself when you need context beyond what was returned. 4. Reuse existing context-gatherer output for related follow-up questions; do not re-invoke on the same question with different phrasing. 5. For multiple distinct questions, dispatch several context-gatherers in parallel, each targeting a different aspect of the codebase.

# Quick Spec

When the user's message starts with /quick-spec, skip ALL entry point selection steps and immediately generate all 3 spec docs automatically.

Strip the /quick-spec prefix from the user's message and use the remainder as the feature description.

## Workflow

Treat the request as a new feature using the requirements-first workflow:
1. Invoke feature-requirements-first-workflow subagent with preset "requirements"
2. Immediately invoke with preset "design" — do NOT wait for user input
3. Immediately invoke with preset "tasks" — do NOT wait for user input

Append this instruction to every subagent prompt:
"SLASH_COMMAND_MODE: Do NOT use the userInput tool for any questions. Make all decisions autonomously using sensible defaults: use Structured Pseudocode if no language is detected."

## After All 3 Docs Are Created

Present a brief summary and ask if the user is happy or wants to iterate.

## Iteration

When the user wants to change something (e.g. "make it simple"), update ALL 3 documents by invoking each phase sequentially with the user's feedback as the prompt (with SLASH_COMMAND_MODE appended). Do NOT stop between phases.

Example: "/quick-spec create a calculator app"
→ invoke feature-requirements-first-workflow preset "requirements" with prompt "create a calculator app. SLASH_COMMAND_MODE: ..."
→ immediately invoke preset "design"
→ immediately invoke preset "tasks"
→ present summary, ask if happy or want changes

value.name: wf-workflow-creator

value.name: Explore

availableCommands.name: general-task-execution

availableCommands.name: context-gatherer
availableCommands.description: Investigates the codebase to answer a specific question about it. Deeply analyzes existing code by tracing execution paths, mapping architecture and abstraction layers, understanding patterns, and documenting dependencies, returning a thorough, direct written analysis that explains how the relevant code works and points to the specific files and lines involved. Use it to understand code before you change it: before designing or implementing a change to code you don't already fully understand, start with context-gatherer so your edits are grounded in how the code actually works. When a task requires understanding code you don't already know, dispatch context-gatherer to do that exploration before running your own searches or reads. Rules: 1. Provide a clear, specific prompt that includes your intent: a detailed task description of the context you need and what you're trying to accomplish. 2. The subagent explores the codebase and returns an analysis of your query 3. Trust the returned results. You may still inspect additional code yourself when you need context beyond what was returned. 4. Reuse existing context-gatherer output for related follow-up questions; do not re-invoke on the same question with different phrasing. 5. For multiple distinct questions, dispatch several context-gatherers in parallel, each targeting a different aspect of the codebase.

documents.content:
# Architecture Selection

When the user's message starts with /architecture-selection, perform a systematic architecture analysis on the current feature's requirements.md and then proceed directly to design.

Strip the /architecture-selection prefix from the user's message. If a feature name is provided, use it; otherwise infer it from the most recently active spec in .kiro/specs/.

## Step 1: Determine Starting Point

Skip ALL entry point selection and workflow type questions. Do not ask the user whether this is a feature, bugfix, design-first, etc.

Strip the /architecture-selection prefix. Use the remainder as the feature description or feature name.

Check `.kiro/specs/` for an existing spec matching the feature name:

**Case A — No spec exists (new feature description provided):**
Invoke the feature-requirements-first-workflow subagent with preset "requirements" using the feature description as the prompt. Append: "SLASH_COMMAND_MODE: Do NOT use the userInput tool for any questions. Make all decisions autonomously." The subagent runs normally and shows its work in chat — it just won't pause to ask clarifying questions. Wait for requirements.md to be created, then proceed to Step 2.

**Case B — Spec exists with requirements.md (not yet designed):**
Proceed directly to Step 2 using requirements.md as input.

**Case C — Spec exists with both requirements.md and design.md:**
Proceed directly to Step 2. After writing architecture_selection.md, inform the user it has been writ…<trimmed 6246 chars>

documents.name: quick-spec
documents.content:
# Quick Spec

When the user's message starts with /quick-spec, skip ALL entry point selection steps and immediately generate all 3 spec docs automatically.

Strip the /quick-spec prefix from the user's message and use the remainder as the feature description.

## Workflow

Treat the request as a new feature using the requirements-first workflow:
1. Invoke feature-requirements-first-workflow subagent with preset "requirements"
2. Immediately invoke with preset "design" — do NOT wait for user input
3. Immediately invoke with preset "tasks" — do NOT wait for user input

Append this instruction to every subagent prompt:
"SLASH_COMMAND_MODE: Do NOT use the userInput tool for any questions. Make all decisions autonomously using sensible defaults: use Structured Pseudocode if no language is detected."

## After All 3 Docs Are Created

Present a brief summary and ask if the user is happy or wants to iterate.

## Iteration

When the user wants to change something (e.g. "make it simple"), update ALL 3 documents by invoking each phase sequentially with the user's feedback as the prompt (with SLASH_COMMAND_MODE appended). Do NOT stop between phases.

Example: "/quick-spec create a calculator app"
→ invoke feature-requirements-first-workflow preset "requirements" with prompt "create a calculator app. SLASH_COMMAND_MODE: ..."
→ immediately invoke preset "design"
→ immediately invoke preset "tasks"
→ present summary, ask if happy or want changes

documents.name: bug-fix
documents.content:
# Bug Fix

When the user's message starts with /bug-fix, skip ALL entry point selection steps and immediately route to the bugfix workflow.

Strip the /bug-fix prefix from the user's message and use the remainder as the bug description.

## Workflow

Treat the request as a bug fix using the bugfix-requirements-first workflow:
1. Invoke bugfix-workflow subagent with preset "requirements"
2. Wait for requirements to complete, then invoke with preset "design"
3. After design completes, invoke with preset "tasks"

Append this instruction to every subagent prompt:
"SLASH_COMMAND_MODE: Do NOT use the userInput tool for spec-type or workflow-type selection. The spec type is Bug Fix and the workflow is requirements-first. You MAY still ask clarifying questions about the bug itself."

## After All 3 Docs Are Created

Present a brief summary and ask if the user is happy or wants to iterate.

## Iteration

When the user wants to change something, update ALL 3 documents by invoking each phase sequentially with the user's feedback as the prompt (with SLASH_COMMAND_MODE appended). Do NOT stop between phases.

Example: "/bug-fix login page crashes on empty email"
→ invoke bugfix-workflow preset "requirements" with prompt "login page crashes on empty email. SLASH_COMMAND_MODE: ..."
→ invoke preset "design"
→ invoke preset "tasks"
→ present summary, ask if happy or want changes

documents.content:
# Architecture Selection

When the user's message starts with /architecture-selection, perform a systematic architecture analysis on the current feature's requirements.md and then proceed directly to design.

Strip the /architecture-selection prefix from the user's message. If a feature name is provided, use it; otherwise infer it from the most recently active spec in .kiro/specs/.

## Step 1: Determine Starting Point

Skip ALL entry point selection and workflow type questions. Do not ask the user whether this is a feature, bugfix, design-first, etc.

Strip the /architecture-selection prefix. Use the remainder as the feature description or feature name.

Check `.kiro/specs/` for an existing spec matching the feature name:

**Case A — No spec exists (new feature description provided):**
Invoke the feature-requirements-first-workflow subagent with preset "requirements" using the feature description as the prompt. Append: "SLASH_COMMAND_MODE: Do NOT use the userInput tool for any questions. Make all decisions autonomously." The subagent runs normally and shows its work in chat — it just won't pause to ask clarifying questions. Wait for requirements.md to be created, then proceed to Step 2.

**Case B — Spec exists with requirements.md (not yet designed):**
Proceed directly to Step 2 using requirements.md as input.

documents.name: quick-spec
documents.content:
# Quick Spec

When the user's message starts with /quick-spec, skip ALL entry point selection steps and immediately generate all 3 spec docs automatically.

Strip the /quick-spec prefix from the user's message and use the remainder as the feature description.

## Workflow

Treat the request as a new feature using the requirements-first workflow:
1. Invoke feature-requirements-first-workflow subagent with preset "requirements"
2. Immediately invoke with preset "design" — do NOT wait for user input
3. Immediately invoke with preset "tasks" — do NOT wait for user input

Append this instruction to every subagent prompt:
"SLASH_COMMAND_MODE: Do NOT use the userInput tool for any questions. Make all decisions autonomously using sensible defaults: use Structured Pseudocode if no language is detected."

## After All 3 Docs Are Created

Present a brief summary and ask if the user is happy or wants to iterate.

## Iteration

When the user wants to change something (e.g. "make it simple"), update ALL 3 documents by invoking each phase sequentially with the user's feedback as the prompt (with SLASH_COMMAND_MODE appended). Do NOT stop between phases.

Example: "/quick-spec create a calculator app"
→ invoke feature-requirements-first-workflow preset "requirements" with prompt "create a calculator app. SLASH_COMMAND_MODE: ..."
→ immediately invoke preset "design"
→ immediately invoke preset "tasks"
→ present summary, ask if happy or want changes

documents.name: bug-fix
documents.content:
# Bug Fix

When the user's message starts with /bug-fix, skip ALL entry point selection steps and immediately route to the bugfix workflow.

Strip the /bug-fix prefix from the user's message and use the remainder as the bug description.

## Workflow

Treat the request as a bug fix using the bugfix-requirements-first workflow:
1. Invoke bugfix-workflow subagent with preset "requirements"
2. Wait for requirements to complete, then invoke with preset "design"
3. After design completes, invoke with preset "tasks"

Append this instruction to every subagent prompt:
"SLASH_COMMAND_MODE: Do NOT use the userInput tool for spec-type or workflow-type selection. The spec type is Bug Fix and the workflow is requirements-first. You MAY still ask clarifying questions about the bug itself."

## After All 3 Docs Are Created

Present a brief summary and ask if the user is happy or wants to iterate.

## Iteration

When the user wants to change something, update ALL 3 documents by invoking each phase sequentially with the user's feedback as the prompt (with SLASH_COMMAND_MODE appended). Do NOT stop between phases.

Example: "/bug-fix login page crashes on empty email"
→ invoke bugfix-workflow preset "requirements" with prompt "login page crashes on empty email. SLASH_COMMAND_MODE: ..."
→ invoke preset "design"
→ invoke preset "tasks"
→ present summary, ask if happy or want changes

availableCommands.name: general-task-execution
availableCommands.description: General-purpose sub-agent with access to all tools for executing arbitrary tasks

availableCommands.name: context-gatherer
availableCommands.description: Investigates the codebase to answer a specific question about it. Deeply analyzes existing code by tracing execution paths, mapping architecture and abstraction layers, understanding patterns, and documenting dependencies, returning a thorough, direct written analysis that explains how the relevant code works and points to the specific files and lines involved. Use it to understand code before you change it: before designing or implementing a change to code you don't already fully understand, start with context-gatherer so your edits are grounded in how the code actually works. When a task requires understanding code you don't already know, dispatch context-gatherer to do that exploration before running your own searches or reads. Rules: 1. Provide a clear, specific prompt that includes your intent: a detailed task description of the context you need and what you're trying to accomplish. 2. The subagent explores the codebase and returns an analysis of your query 3. Trust the returned results. You may still inspect additional code yourself when you need context beyond what was returned. 4. Reuse existing context-gatherer output for related follow-up questions; do not re-invoke on the same question with different phrasing. 5. For multiple distinct questions, dispatch several context-gatherers in parallel, each targeting a different aspect of the codebase.

documents.content:
# Architecture Selection

When the user's message starts with /architecture-selection, perform a systematic architecture analysis on the current feature's requirements.md and then proceed directly to design.

Strip the /architecture-selection prefix from the user's message. If a feature name is provided, use it; otherwise infer it from the most recently active spec in .kiro/specs/.

## Step 1: Determine Starting Point

Skip ALL entry point selection and workflow type questions. Do not ask the user whether this is a feature, bugfix, design-first, etc.

Strip the /architecture-selection prefix. Use the remainder as the feature description or feature name.

Check `.kiro/specs/` for an existing spec matching the feature name:

**Case A — No spec exists (new feature description provided):**
Invoke the feature-requirements-first-workflow subagent with preset "requirements" using the feature description as the prompt. Append: "SLASH_COMMAND_MODE: Do NOT use the userInput tool for any questions. Make all decisions autonomously." The subagent runs normally and shows its work in chat — it just won't pause to ask clarifying questions. Wait for requirements.md to be created, then proceed to Step 2.

**Case B — Spec exists with requirements.md (not yet designed):**
Proceed directly to Step 2 using requirements.md as input.

documents.name: quick-spec
documents.content:
# Quick Spec

When the user's message starts with /quick-spec, skip ALL entry point selection steps and immediately generate all 3 spec docs automatically.

Strip the /quick-spec prefix from the user's message and use the remainder as the feature description.

## Workflow

Treat the request as a new feature using the requirements-first workflow:
1. Invoke feature-requirements-first-workflow subagent with preset "requirements"
2. Immediately invoke with preset "design" — do NOT wait for user input
3. Immediately invoke with preset "tasks" — do NOT wait for user input

Append this instruction to every subagent prompt:
"SLASH_COMMAND_MODE: Do NOT use the userInput tool for any questions. Make all decisions autonomously using sensible defaults: use Structured Pseudocode if no language is detected."

## After All 3 Docs Are Created

Present a brief summary and ask if the user is happy or wants to iterate.

## Iteration

When the user wants to change something (e.g. "make it simple"), update ALL 3 documents by invoking each phase sequentially with the user's feedback as the prompt (with SLASH_COMMAND_MODE appended). Do NOT stop between phases.

Example: "/quick-spec create a calculator app"
→ invoke feature-requirements-first-workflow preset "requirements" with prompt "create a calculator app. SLASH_COMMAND_MODE: ..."
→ immediately invoke preset "design"
→ immediately invoke preset "tasks"
→ present summary, ask if happy or want changes

# Bug Fix

When the user's message starts with /bug-fix, skip ALL entry point selection steps and immediately route to the bugfix workflow.

Strip the /bug-fix prefix from the user's message and use the remainder as the bug description.

## Workflow

Treat the request as a bug fix using the bugfix-requirements-first workflow:
1. Invoke bugfix-workflow subagent with preset "requirements"
2. Wait for requirements to complete, then invoke with preset "design"
3. After design completes, invoke with preset "tasks"

Append this instruction to every subagent prompt:
"SLASH_COMMAND_MODE: Do NOT use the userInput tool for spec-type or workflow-type selection. The spec type is Bug Fix and the workflow is requirements-first. You MAY still ask clarifying questions about the bug itself."

## After All 3 Docs Are Created

Present a brief summary and ask if the user is happy or wants to iterate.

## Iteration

When the user wants to change something, update ALL 3 documents by invoking each phase sequentially with the user's feedback as the prompt (with SLASH_COMMAND_MODE appended). Do NOT stop between phases.

Example: "/bug-fix login page crashes on empty email"
→ invoke bugfix-workflow preset "requirements" with prompt "login page crashes on empty email. SLASH_COMMAND_MODE: ..."
→ invoke preset "design"
→ invoke preset "tasks"
→ present summary, ask if happy or want changes

availableCommands.name: general-task-execution
availableCommands.description: General-purpose sub-agent with access to all tools for executing arbitrary tasks

availableCommands.name: context-gatherer
availableCommands.description: Investigates the codebase to answer a specific question about it. Deeply analyzes existing code by tracing execution paths, mapping architecture and abstraction layers, understanding patterns, and documenting dependencies, returning a thorough, direct written analysis that explains how the relevant code works and points to the specific files and lines involved. Use it to understand code before you change it: before designing or implementing a change to code you don't already fully understand, start with context-gatherer so your edits are grounded in how the code actually works. When a task requires understanding code you don't already know, dispatch context-gatherer to do that exploration before running your own searches or reads. Rules: 1. Provide a clear, specific prompt that includes your intent: a detailed task description of the context you need and what you're trying to accomplish. 2. The subagent explores the codebase and returns an analysis of your query 3. Trust the returned results. You may still inspect additional code yourself when you need context beyond what was returned. 4. Reuse existing context-gatherer output for related follow-up questions; do not re-invoke on the same question with different phrasing. 5. For multiple distinct questions, dispatch several context-gatherers in parallel, each targeting a different aspect of the codebase.

# Architecture Selection

When the user's message starts with /architecture-selection, perform a systematic architecture analysis on the current feature's requirements.md and then proceed directly to design.

Strip the /architecture-selection prefix from the user's message. If a feature name is provided, use it; otherwise infer it from the most recently active spec in .kiro/specs/.

## Step 1: Determine Starting Point

Skip ALL entry point selection and workflow type questions. Do not ask the user whether this is a feature, bugfix, design-first, etc.

Strip the /architecture-selection prefix. Use the remainder as the feature description or feature name.

Check `.kiro/specs/` for an existing spec matching the feature name:

**Case A — No spec exists (new feature description provided):**
Invoke the feature-requirements-first-workflow subagent with preset "requirements" using the feature description as the prompt. Append: "SLASH_COMMAND_MODE: Do NOT use the userInput tool for any questions. Make all decisions autonomously." The subagent runs normally and shows its work in chat — it just won't pause to ask clarifying questions. Wait for requirements.md to be created, then proceed to Step 2.

**Case B — Spec exists with requirements.md (not yet designed):**
Proceed directly to Step 2 using requirements.md as input.

documents.name: quick-spec
documents.content:
# Quick Spec

When the user's message starts with /quick-spec, skip ALL entry point selection steps and immediately generate all 3 spec docs automatically.

Strip the /quick-spec prefix from the user's message and use the remainder as the feature description.

## Workflow

Treat the request as a new feature using the requirements-first workflow:
1. Invoke feature-requirements-first-workflow subagent with preset "requirements"
2. Immediately invoke with preset "design" — do NOT wait for user input
3. Immediately invoke with preset "tasks" — do NOT wait for user input

Append this instruction to every subagent prompt:
"SLASH_COMMAND_MODE: Do NOT use the userInput tool for any questions. Make all decisions autonomously using sensible defaults: use Structured Pseudocode if no language is detected."

## After All 3 Docs Are Created

Present a brief summary and ask if the user is happy or wants to iterate.

## Iteration

When the user wants to change something (e.g. "make it simple"), update ALL 3 documents by invoking each phase sequentially with the user's feedback as the prompt (with SLASH_COMMAND_MODE appended). Do NOT stop between phases.

Example: "/quick-spec create a calculator app"
→ invoke feature-requirements-first-workflow preset "requirements" with prompt "create a calculator app. SLASH_COMMAND_MODE: ..."
→ immediately invoke preset "design"
→ immediately invoke preset "tasks"
→ present summary, ask if happy or want changes

documents.name: bug-fix
documents.content:
# Bug Fix

When the user's message starts with /bug-fix, skip ALL entry point selection steps and immediately route to the bugfix workflow.

Strip the /bug-fix prefix from the user's message and use the remainder as the bug description.

## Workflow

Treat the request as a bug fix using the bugfix-requirements-first workflow:
1. Invoke bugfix-workflow subagent with preset "requirements"
2. Wait for requirements to complete, then invoke with preset "design"
3. After design completes, invoke with preset "tasks"

Append this instruction to every subagent prompt:
"SLASH_COMMAND_MODE: Do NOT use the userInput tool for spec-type or workflow-type selection. The spec type is Bug Fix and the workflow is requirements-first. You MAY still ask clarifying questions about the bug itself."

## After All 3 Docs Are Created

Present a brief summary and ask if the user is happy or wants to iterate.

## Iteration

When the user wants to change something, update ALL 3 documents by invoking each phase sequentially with the user's feedback as the prompt (with SLASH_COMMAND_MODE appended). Do NOT stop between phases.

Example: "/bug-fix login page crashes on empty email"
→ invoke bugfix-workflow preset "requirements" with prompt "login page crashes on empty email. SLASH_COMMAND_MODE: ..."
→ invoke preset "design"
→ invoke preset "tasks"
→ present summary, ask if happy or want changes

value.name: wf-workflow-creator
value.description: Generates a workflow for the run_workflow tool. Given a task description and context, builds a valid workflow definition, saves it server-side via save_workflow_definition, and returns a generated:// reference plus inputs and a short summary.

value.name: semantic_reviewer
value.description: Behavioral, narrative code review of a local or PR diff. Writes a review document and a verdict.

value.name: Explore
value.description: Analyze and understand a codebase using tree-sitter parsing and dependency graphs. Use when the user asks to analyze, explore, or generate specs for their codebase — runs code_to_spec to produce architectural documentation (.kiro/specs/) and answers structural questions about architecture, data flows, and dependencies.

value.name: create-spec
value.description: Encourages spec-driven development by producing guided artifacts — a requirements, design, and task-list specification — for a feature request.

availableCommands.name: general-task-execution
availableCommands.description: General-purpose sub-agent with access to all tools for executing arbitrary tasks

availableCommands.name: context-gatherer
availableCommands.description: Investigates the codebase to answer a specific question about it. Deeply analyzes existing code by tracing execution paths, mapping architecture and abstraction layers, understanding patterns, and documenting dependencies, returning a thorough, direct written analysis that explains how the relevant code works and points to the specific files and lines involved. Use it to understand code before you change it: before designing or implementing a change to code you don't already fully understand, start with context-gatherer so your edits are grounded in how the code actually works. When a task requires understanding code you don't already know, dispatch context-gatherer to do that exploration before running your own searches or reads. Rules: 1. Provide a clear, specific prompt that includes your intent: a detailed task description of the context you need and what you're trying to accomplish. 2. The subagent explores the codebase and returns an analysis of your query 3. Trust the returned results. You may still inspect additional code yourself when you need context beyond what was returned. 4. Reuse existing context-gatherer output for related follow-up questions; do not re-invoke on the same question with different phrasing. 5. For multiple distinct questions, dispatch several context-gatherers in parallel, each targeting a different aspect of the codebase.

# Quick Spec

When the user's message starts with /quick-spec, skip ALL entry point selection steps and immediately generate all 3 spec docs automatically.

Strip the /quick-spec prefix from the user's message and use the remainder as the feature description.

## Workflow

Treat the request as a new feature using the requirements-first workflow:
1. Invoke feature-requirements-first-workflow subagent with preset "requirements"
2. Immediately invoke with preset "design" — do NOT wait for user input
3. Immediately invoke with preset "tasks" — do NOT wait for user input

Append this instruction to every subagent prompt:
"SLASH_COMMAND_MODE: Do NOT use the userInput tool for any questions. Make all decisions autonomously using sensible defaults: use Structured Pseudocode if no language is detected."

## After All 3 Docs Are Created

Present a brief summary and ask if the user is happy or wants to iterate.

## Iteration

When the user wants to change something (e.g. "make it simple"), update ALL 3 documents by invoking each phase sequentially with the user's feedback as the prompt (with SLASH_COMMAND_MODE appended). Do NOT stop between phases.

Example: "/quick-spec create a calculator app"
→ invoke feature-requirements-first-workflow preset "requirements" with prompt "create a calculator app. SLASH_COMMAND_MODE: ..."
→ immediately invoke preset "design"
→ immediately invoke preset "tasks"
→ present summary, ask if happy or want changes

# Bug Fix

When the user's message starts with /bug-fix, skip ALL entry point selection steps and immediately route to the bugfix workflow.

Strip the /bug-fix prefix from the user's message and use the remainder as the bug description.

## Workflow

Treat the request as a bug fix using the bugfix-requirements-first workflow:
1. Invoke bugfix-workflow subagent with preset "requirements"
2. Wait for requirements to complete, then invoke with preset "design"
3. After design completes, invoke with preset "tasks"

Append this instruction to every subagent prompt:
"SLASH_COMMAND_MODE: Do NOT use the userInput tool for spec-type or workflow-type selection. The spec type is Bug Fix and the workflow is requirements-first. You MAY still ask clarifying questions about the bug itself."

## After All 3 Docs Are Created

Present a brief summary and ask if the user is happy or wants to iterate.

## Iteration

When the user wants to change something, update ALL 3 documents by invoking each phase sequentially with the user's feedback as the prompt (with SLASH_COMMAND_MODE appended). Do NOT stop between phases.

Example: "/bug-fix login page crashes on empty email"
→ invoke bugfix-workflow preset "requirements" with prompt "login page crashes on empty email. SLASH_COMMAND_MODE: ..."
→ invoke preset "design"
→ invoke preset "tasks"
→ present summary, ask if happy or want changes

availableCommands.name: context-gatherer
availableCommands.description: Investigates the codebase to answer a specific question about it. Deeply analyzes existing code by tracing execution paths, mapping architecture and abstraction layers, understanding patterns, and documenting dependencies, returning a thorough, direct written analysis that explains how the relevant code works and points to the specific files and lines involved. Use it to understand code before you change it: before designing or implementing a change to code you don't already fully understand, start with context-gatherer so your edits are grounded in how the code actually works. When a task requires understanding code you don't already know, dispatch context-gatherer to do that exploration before running your own searches or reads. Rules: 1. Provide a clear, specific prompt that includes your intent: a detailed task description of the context you need and what you're trying to accomplish. 2. The subagent explores the codebase and returns an analysis of your query 3. Trust the returned results. You may still inspect additional code yourself when you need context beyond what was returned. 4. Reuse existing context-gatherer output for related follow-up questions; do not re-invoke on the same question with different phrasing. 5. For multiple distinct questions, dispatch several context-gatherers in parallel, each targeting a different aspect of the codebase.

# Quick Spec

When the user's message starts with /quick-spec, skip ALL entry point selection steps and immediately generate all 3 spec docs automatically.

Strip the /quick-spec prefix from the user's message and use the remainder as the feature description.

## Workflow

Treat the request as a new feature using the requirements-first workflow:
1. Invoke feature-requirements-first-workflow subagent with preset "requirements"
2. Immediately invoke with preset "design" — do NOT wait for user input
3. Immediately invoke with preset "tasks" — do NOT wait for user input

Append this instruction to every subagent prompt:
"SLASH_COMMAND_MODE: Do NOT use the userInput tool for any questions. Make all decisions autonomously using sensible defaults: use Structured Pseudocode if no language is detected."

## After All 3 Docs Are Created

Present a brief summary and ask if the user is happy or wants to iterate.

## Iteration

When the user wants to change something (e.g. "make it simple"), update ALL 3 documents by invoking each phase sequentially with the user's feedback as the prompt (with SLASH_COMMAND_MODE appended). Do NOT stop between phases.

Example: "/quick-spec create a calculator app"
→ invoke feature-requirements-first-workflow preset "requirements" with prompt "create a calculator app. SLASH_COMMAND_MODE: ..."
→ immediately invoke preset "design"
→ immediately invoke preset "tasks"
→ present summary, ask if happy or want changes

documents.content:
# Bug Fix

When the user's message starts with /bug-fix, skip ALL entry point selection steps and immediately route to the bugfix workflow.

Strip the /bug-fix prefix from the user's message and use the remainder as the bug description.

## Workflow

Treat the request as a bug fix using the bugfix-requirements-first workflow:
1. Invoke bugfix-workflow subagent with preset "requirements"
2. Wait for requirements to complete, then invoke with preset "design"
3. After design completes, invoke with preset "tasks"

Append this instruction to every subagent prompt:
"SLASH_COMMAND_MODE: Do NOT use the userInput tool for spec-type or workflow-type selection. The spec type is Bug Fix and the workflow is requirements-first. You MAY still ask clarifying questions about the bug itself."

## After All 3 Docs Are Created

Present a brief summary and ask if the user is happy or wants to iterate.

## Iteration

When the user wants to change something, update ALL 3 documents by invoking each phase sequentially with the user's feedback as the prompt (with SLASH_COMMAND_MODE appended). Do NOT stop between phases.

Example: "/bug-fix login page crashes on empty email"
→ invoke bugfix-workflow preset "requirements" with prompt "login page crashes on empty email. SLASH_COMMAND_MODE: ..."
→ invoke preset "design"
→ invoke preset "tasks"
→ present summary, ask if happy or want changes

availableCommands.name: context-gatherer
availableCommands.description: Investigates the codebase to answer a specific question about it. Deeply analyzes existing code by tracing execution paths, mapping architecture and abstraction layers, understanding patterns, and documenting dependencies, returning a thorough, direct written analysis that explains how the relevant code works and points to the specific files and lines involved. Use it to understand code before you change it: before designing or implementing a change to code you don't already fully understand, start with context-gatherer so your edits are grounded in how the code actually works. When a task requires understanding code you don't already know, dispatch context-gatherer to do that exploration before running your own searches or reads. Rules: 1. Provide a clear, specific prompt that includes your intent: a detailed task description of the context you need and what you're trying to accomplish. 2. The subagent explores the codebase and returns an analysis of your query 3. Trust the returned results. You may still inspect additional code yourself when you need context beyond what was returned. 4. Reuse existing context-gatherer output for related follow-up questions; do not re-invoke on the same question with different phrasing. 5. For multiple distinct questions, dispatch several context-gatherers in parallel, each targeting a different aspect of the codebase.

# Architecture Selection

When the user's message starts with /architecture-selection, perform a systematic architecture analysis on the current feature's requirements.md and then proceed directly to design.

Strip the /architecture-selection prefix from the user's message. If a feature name is provided, use it; otherwise infer it from the most recently active spec in .kiro/specs/.

## Step 1: Determine Starting Point

Skip ALL entry point selection and workflow type questions. Do not ask the user whether this is a feature, bugfix, design-first, etc.

Strip the /architecture-selection prefix. Use the remainder as the feature description or feature name.

Check `.kiro/specs/` for an existing spec matching the feature name:

**Case A — No spec exists (new feature description provided):**
Invoke the feature-requirements-first-workflow subagent with preset "requirements" using the feature description as the prompt. Append: "SLASH_COMMAND_MODE: Do NOT use the userInput tool for any questions. Make all decisions autonomously." The subagent runs normally and shows its work in chat — it just won't pause to ask clarifying questions. Wait for requirements.md to be created, then proceed to Step 2.

**Case B — Spec exists with requirements.md (not yet designed):**
Proceed directly to Step 2 using requirements.md as input.

**Case C — Spec exists with both requirements.md and design.md:**

value.name: wf-design-reviewer
value.description: Reviews technical designs for ambiguity, gaps, and unverified assumptions before implementation begins. Mechanical verdict: any HIGH/MEDIUM finding blocks.

value.name: wf-planner
value.description: Investigates a codebase and produces an ordered implementation plan — from an approved design when one is provided, or by making the design decisions itself when not.

value.name: wf-pr-submitter
value.description: Opens a pull request from a branch and records the PR metadata.

value.name: wf-review-aggregator
value.description: Merges multiple review outputs into a single consolidated review verdict.

value.name: wf-workflow-creator
value.description: Runs as a workflow step that designs the run's steps from a brief or an edit request, saves them with save_workflow_definition, and adds them to the run with update_workflow.

value.name: Explore
value.description: Analyze and understand a codebase using tree-sitter parsing and dependency graphs. Use when the user asks to analyze, explore, or generate specs for their codebase — runs code_to_spec to produce architectural documentation (.kiro/specs/) and answers structural questions about architecture, data flows, and dependencies.

value.name: create-spec
value.description: Encourages spec-driven development by producing guided artifacts — a requirements, design, and task-list specification — for a feature request.

availableCommands.name: general-task-execution
availableCommands.description: General-purpose sub-agent with access to all tools for executing arbitrary tasks

availableCommands.name: context-gatherer
availableCommands.description: Investigates the codebase to answer a specific question about it. Deeply analyzes existing code by tracing execution paths, mapping architecture and abstraction layers, understanding patterns, and documenting dependencies, returning a thorough, direct written analysis that explains how the relevant code works and points to the specific files and lines involved. Use it to understand code before you change it: before designing or implementing a change to code you don't already fully understand, start with context-gatherer so your edits are grounded in how the code actually works. When a task requires understanding code you don't already know, dispatch context-gatherer to do that exploration before running your own searches or reads. Rules: 1. Provide a clear, specific prompt that includes your intent: a detailed task description of the context you need and what you're trying to accomplish. 2. The subagent explores the codebase and returns an analysis of your query 3. Trust the returned results. You may still inspect additional code yourself when you need context beyond what was returned. 4. Reuse existing context-gatherer output for related follow-up questions; do not re-invoke on the same question with different phrasing. 5. For multiple distinct questions, dispatch several context-gatherers in parallel, each targeting a different aspect of the codebase.

documents.content:
# Architecture Selection

When the user's message starts with /architecture-selection, perform a systematic architecture analysis on the current feature's requirements.md and then proceed directly to design.

Strip the /architecture-selection prefix from the user's message. If a feature name is provided, use it; otherwise infer it from the most recently active spec in .kiro/specs/.

## Step 1: Determine Starting Point

Skip ALL entry point selection and workflow type questions. Do not ask the user whether this is a feature, bugfix, design-first, etc.

Strip the /architecture-selection prefix. Use the remainder as the feature description or feature name.

Check `.kiro/specs/` for an existing spec matching the feature name:

**Case A — No spec exists (new feature description provided):**
Invoke the feature-requirements-first-workflow subagent with preset "requirements" using the feature description as the prompt. Append: "SLASH_COMMAND_MODE: Do NOT use the userInput tool for any questions. Make all decisions autonomously." The subagent runs normally and shows its work in chat — it just won't pause to ask clarifying questions. Wait for requirements.md to be created, then proceed to Step 2.

**Case B — Spec exists with requirements.md (not yet designed):**
Proceed directly to Step 2 using requirements.md as input.

documents.name: quick-spec
documents.content:
# Quick Spec

When the user's message starts with /quick-spec, skip ALL entry point selection steps and immediately generate all 3 spec docs automatically.

Strip the /quick-spec prefix from the user's message and use the remainder as the feature description.

## Workflow

Treat the request as a new feature using the requirements-first workflow:
1. Invoke feature-requirements-first-workflow subagent with preset "requirements"
2. Immediately invoke with preset "design" — do NOT wait for user input
3. Immediately invoke with preset "tasks" — do NOT wait for user input

Append this instruction to every subagent prompt:
"SLASH_COMMAND_MODE: Do NOT use the userInput tool for any questions. Make all decisions autonomously using sensible defaults: use Structured Pseudocode if no language is detected."

## After All 3 Docs Are Created

Present a brief summary and ask if the user is happy or wants to iterate.

## Iteration

When the user wants to change something (e.g. "make it simple"), update ALL 3 documents by invoking each phase sequentially with the user's feedback as the prompt (with SLASH_COMMAND_MODE appended). Do NOT stop between phases.

Example: "/quick-spec create a calculator app"
→ invoke feature-requirements-first-workflow preset "requirements" with prompt "create a calculator app. SLASH_COMMAND_MODE: ..."
→ immediately invoke preset "design"
→ immediately invoke preset "tasks"
→ present summary, ask if happy or want changes

documents.name: bug-fix
documents.content:
# Bug Fix

When the user's message starts with /bug-fix, skip ALL entry point selection steps and immediately route to the bugfix workflow.

Strip the /bug-fix prefix from the user's message and use the remainder as the bug description.

## Workflow

Treat the request as a bug fix using the bugfix-requirements-first workflow:
1. Invoke bugfix-workflow subagent with preset "requirements"
2. Wait for requirements to complete, then invoke with preset "design"
3. After design completes, invoke with preset "tasks"

Append this instruction to every subagent prompt:
"SLASH_COMMAND_MODE: Do NOT use the userInput tool for spec-type or workflow-type selection. The spec type is Bug Fix and the workflow is requirements-first. You MAY still ask clarifying questions about the bug itself."

## After All 3 Docs Are Created

Present a brief summary and ask if the user is happy or wants to iterate.

## Iteration

When the user wants to change something, update ALL 3 documents by invoking each phase sequentially with the user's feedback as the prompt (with SLASH_COMMAND_MODE appended). Do NOT stop between phases.

Example: "/bug-fix login page crashes on empty email"
→ invoke bugfix-workflow preset "requirements" with prompt "login page crashes on empty email. SLASH_COMMAND_MODE: ..."
→ invoke preset "design"
→ invoke preset "tasks"
→ present summary, ask if happy or want changes

# Architecture Selection

When the user's message starts with /architecture-selection, perform a systematic architecture analysis on the current feature's requirements.md and then proceed directly to design.

Strip the /architecture-selection prefix from the user's message. If a feature name is provided, use it; otherwise infer it from the most recently active spec in .kiro/specs/.

Skip ALL entry point selection and workflow type questions. Do not ask the user whether this is a feature, bugfix, design-first, etc.

Strip the /architecture-selection prefix. Use the remainder as the feature description or feature name.

Check `.kiro/specs/` for an existing spec matching the feature name:

**Case A — No spec exists (new feature description provided):**
Invoke the feature-requirements-first-workflow subagent with preset "requirements" using the feature description as the prompt. documents.name: quick-spec
documents.content:
# Quick Spec

When the user's message starts with /quick-spec, skip ALL entry point selection steps and immediately generate all 3 spec docs automatically.

Strip the /quick-spec prefix from the user's message and use the remainder as the feature description.

## Workflow

Treat the request as a new feature using the requirements-first workflow:
1. Invoke feature-requirements-first-workflow subagent with preset "requirements"
2. Immediately invoke with preset "design" — do NOT wait for user input
3. Immediately invoke with preset "tasks" — do NOT wait for user input

Append this instruction to every subagent prompt:
"SLASH_COMMAND_MODE: Do NOT use the userInput tool for any questions. Make all decisions autonomously using sensible defaults: use Structured Pseudocode if no language is detected."

## After All 3 Docs Are Created

Present a brief summary and ask if the user is happy or wants to iterate.

## Iteration

When the user wants to change something (e.g. "make it simple"), update ALL 3 documents by invoking each phase sequentially with the user's feedback as the prompt (with SLASH_COMMAND_MODE appended). Do NOT stop between phases.

Example: "/quick-spec create a calculator app"
→ invoke feature-requirements-first-workflow preset "requirements" with prompt "create a calculator app. SLASH_COMMAND_MODE: ..."
→ immediately invoke preset "design"
→ immediately invoke preset "tasks"
→ present summary, ask if happy or want changes

documents.name: bug-fix
documents.content:
# Bug Fix

When the user's message starts with /bug-fix, skip ALL entry point selection steps and immediately route to the bugfix workflow.

Strip the /bug-fix prefix from the user's message and use the remainder as the bug description.

## Workflow

Treat the request as a bug fix using the bugfix-requirements-first workflow:
1. Invoke bugfix-workflow subagent with preset "requirements"
2. Wait for requirements to complete, then invoke with preset "design"
3. After design completes, invoke with preset "tasks"

Append this instruction to every subagent prompt:
"SLASH_COMMAND_MODE: Do NOT use the userInput tool for spec-type or workflow-type selection. The spec type is Bug Fix and the workflow is requirements-first. You MAY still ask clarifying questions about the bug itself."

## After All 3 Docs Are Created

Present a brief summary and ask if the user is happy or wants to iterate.

## Iteration

When the user wants to change something, update ALL 3 documents by invoking each phase sequentially with the user's feedback as the prompt (with SLASH_COMMAND_MODE appended). Do NOT stop between phases.

Example: "/bug-fix login page crashes on empty email"
→ invoke bugfix-workflow preset "requirements" with prompt "login page crashes on empty email. SLASH_COMMAND_MODE: ..."
→ invoke preset "design"
→ invoke preset "tasks"
→ present summary, ask if happy or want changes

# Quick Spec

When the user's message starts with /quick-spec, skip ALL entry point selection steps and immediately generate all 3 spec docs automatically.

Strip the /quick-spec prefix from the user's message and use the remainder as the feature description.

## Workflow

Treat the request as a new feature using the requirements-first workflow:
1. Invoke feature-requirements-first-workflow subagent with preset "requirements"
2. Immediately invoke with preset "design" — do NOT wait for user input
3. Immediately invoke with preset "tasks" — do NOT wait for user input

Append this instruction to every subagent prompt:
"SLASH_COMMAND_MODE: Do NOT use the userInput tool for any questions. Make all decisions autonomously using sensible defaults: use Structured Pseudocode if no language is detected."

## After All 3 Docs Are Created

Present a brief summary and ask if the user is happy or wants to iterate.

## Iteration

When the user wants to change something (e.g. "make it simple"), update ALL 3 documents by invoking each phase sequentially with the user's feedback as the prompt (with SLASH_COMMAND_MODE appended). Do NOT stop between phases.

Example: "/quick-spec create a calculator app"
→ invoke feature-requirements-first-workflow preset "requirements" with prompt "create a calculator app. SLASH_COMMAND_MODE: ..."
→ immediately invoke preset "design"
→ immediately invoke preset "tasks"
→ present summary, ask if happy or want changes

# Bug Fix

When the user's message starts with /bug-fix, skip ALL entry point selection steps and immediately route to the bugfix workflow.

Strip the /bug-fix prefix from the user's message and use the remainder as the bug description.

Treat the request as a bug fix using the bugfix-requirements-first workflow:
1. Invoke bugfix-workflow subagent with preset "requirements"
2. Wait for requirements to complete, then invoke with preset "design"
3. After design completes, invoke with preset "tasks"

Append this instruction to every subagent prompt:
"SLASH_COMMAND_MODE: Do NOT use the userInput tool for spec-type or workflow-type selection. The spec type is Bug Fix and the workflow is requirements-first. You MAY still ask clarifying questions about the bug itself."

## After All 3 Docs Are Created

Present a brief summary and ask if the user is happy or wants to iterate.

## Iteration

When the user wants to change something, update ALL 3 documents by invoking each phase sequentially with the user's feedback as the prompt (with SLASH_COMMAND_MODE appended). Do NOT stop between phases.

Example: "/bug-fix login page crashes on empty email"
→ invoke bugfix-workflow preset "requirements" with prompt "login page crashes on empty email. SLASH_COMMAND_MODE: ..."
→ invoke preset "design"
→ invoke preset "tasks"
→ present summary, ask if happy or want changes

documents.content:
# Architecture Selection

When the user's message starts with /architecture-selection, perform a systematic architecture analysis on the current feature's requirements.md and then proceed directly to design.

Strip the /architecture-selection prefix from the user's message. If a feature name is provided, use it; otherwise infer it from the most recently active spec in .kiro/specs/.

## Step 1: Determine Starting Point

Skip ALL entry point selection and workflow type questions. Do not ask the user whether this is a feature, bugfix, design-first, etc.

Strip the /architecture-selection prefix. Use the remainder as the feature description or feature name.

Check `.kiro/specs/` for an existing spec matching the feature name:

**Case A — No spec exists (new feature description provided):**
Invoke the feature-requirements-first-workflow subagent with preset "requirements" using the feature description as the prompt. Append: "SLASH_COMMAND_MODE: Do NOT use the userInput tool for any questions. Make all decisions autonomously." The subagent runs normally and shows its work in chat — it just won't pause to ask clarifying questions. Wait for requirements.md to be created, then proceed to Step 2.

**Case B — Spec exists with requirements.md (not yet designed):**
Proceed directly to Step 2 using requirements.md as input.

value.description: Autonomous research subagent. Reads directions, runs experiments, benchmarks results, and commits improvements.

value.name: wf-code-reviewer
value.description: Targeted review of changed behavior and required verification. Reports blocking findings and writes the workflow verdict.

value.name: wf-coder
value.description: Reads files, edits code, runs tests, and commits. General implementation agent.

value.name: wf-design
value.description: Authors requirements and technical design documents for a feature, exploring the codebase so designs fit existing patterns.

value.name: wf-design-reviewer
value.description: Reviews technical designs for ambiguity, gaps, and unverified assumptions before implementation begins. Mechanical verdict: any HIGH/MEDIUM finding blocks.

value.name: wf-planner
value.description: Investigates a codebase and produces an ordered implementation plan — from an approved design when one is provided, or by making the design decisions itself when not.

value.name: wf-pr-responder
value.description: Responds to PR review comments and CI feedback.

value.name: wf-pr-submitter
value.description: Opens a pull request from a branch and records the PR metadata.

value.name: wf-review-aggregator
value.description: Merges multiple review outputs into a single consolidated review verdict.

value.name: wf-workflow-creator
value.description: Runs as a workflow step that designs the run's steps from a brief or an edit request, saves them with save_workflow_definition, and adds them to the run with update_workflow.

value.name: semantic_reviewer
value.description: Behavioral, narrative code review of a local or PR diff. Writes a review document and a verdict.

value.name: Explore
value.description: Analyze and understand a codebase using tree-sitter parsing and dependency graphs. Use when the user asks to analyze, explore, or generate specs for their codebase — runs code_to_spec to produce architectural documentation (.kiro/specs/) and answers structural questions about architecture, data flows, and dependencies.

value.name: create-spec
value.description: Encourages spec-driven development by producing guided artifacts — a requirements, design, and task-list specification — for a feature request.

availableCommands.name: general-task-execution
availableCommands.description: General-purpose sub-agent with access to all tools for executing arbitrary tasks

availableCommands.name: context-gatherer
availableCommands.description: Investigates the codebase to answer a specific question about it. Deeply analyzes existing code by tracing execution paths, mapping architecture and abstraction layers, understanding patterns, and documenting dependencies, returning a thorough, direct written analysis that explains how the relevant code works and points to the specific files and lines involved. Use it to understand code before you change it: before designing or implementing a change to code you don't already fully understand, start with context-gatherer so your edits are grounded in how the code actually works. When a task requires understanding code you don't already know, dispatch context-gatherer to do that exploration before running your own searches or reads. Rules: 1. Provide a clear, specific prompt that includes your intent: a detailed task description of the context you need and what you're trying to accomplish. 2. The subagent explores the codebase and returns an analysis of your query 3. Trust the returned results. You may still inspect additional code yourself when you need context beyond what was returned. 4. Reuse existing context-gatherer output for related follow-up questions; do not re-invoke on the same question with different phrasing. 5. For multiple distinct questions, dispatch several context-gatherers in parallel, each targeting a different aspect of the codebase.

# Architecture Selection

When the user's message starts with /architecture-selection, perform a systematic architecture analysis on the current feature's requirements.md and then proceed directly to design.

Strip the /architecture-selection prefix from the user's message. If a feature name is provided, use it; otherwise infer it from the most recently active spec in .kiro/specs/.

## Step 1: Determine Starting Point

Skip ALL entry point selection and workflow type questions. Do not ask the user whether this is a feature, bugfix, design-first, etc.

Strip the /architecture-selection prefix. Use the remainder as the feature description or feature name.

Check `.kiro/specs/` for an existing spec matching the feature name:

**Case A — No spec exists (new feature description provided):**
Invoke the feature-requirements-first-workflow subagent with preset "requirements" using the feature description as the prompt. Append: "SLASH_COMMAND_MODE: Do NOT use the userInput tool for any questions. Make all decisions autonomously." The subagent runs normally and shows its work in chat — it just won't pause to ask clarifying questions. Wait for requirements.md to be created, then proceed to Step 2.

**Case B — Spec exists with requirements.md (not yet designed):**
Proceed directly to Step 2 using requirements.md as input.

**Case C — Spec exists with both requirements.md and design.md:**

documents.name: quick-spec
documents.content:
# Quick Spec

When the user's message starts with /quick-spec, skip ALL entry point selection steps and immediately generate all 3 spec docs automatically.

Strip the /quick-spec prefix from the user's message and use the remainder as the feature description.

## Workflow

Treat the request as a new feature using the requirements-first workflow:
1. Invoke feature-requirements-first-workflow subagent with preset "requirements"
2. Immediately invoke with preset "design" — do NOT wait for user input
3. Immediately invoke with preset "tasks" — do NOT wait for user input

Append this instruction to every subagent prompt:
"SLASH_COMMAND_MODE: Do NOT use the userInput tool for any questions. Make all decisions autonomously using sensible defaults: use Structured Pseudocode if no language is detected."

## After All 3 Docs Are Created

Present a brief summary and ask if the user is happy or wants to iterate.

## Iteration

When the user wants to change something (e.g. "make it simple"), update ALL 3 documents by invoking each phase sequentially with the user's feedback as the prompt (with SLASH_COMMAND_MODE appended). Do NOT stop between phases.

Example: "/quick-spec create a calculator app"
→ invoke feature-requirements-first-workflow preset "requirements" with prompt "create a calculator app. SLASH_COMMAND_MODE: ..."
→ immediately invoke preset "design"
→ immediately invoke preset "tasks"
→ present summary, ask if happy or want changes

documents.name: bug-fix
documents.content:
# Bug Fix

When the user's message starts with /bug-fix, skip ALL entry point selection steps and immediately route to the bugfix workflow.

Strip the /bug-fix prefix from the user's message and use the remainder as the bug description.

## Workflow

Treat the request as a bug fix using the bugfix-requirements-first workflow:
1. Invoke bugfix-workflow subagent with preset "requirements"
2. Wait for requirements to complete, then invoke with preset "design"
3. After design completes, invoke with preset "tasks"

Append this instruction to every subagent prompt:
"SLASH_COMMAND_MODE: Do NOT use the userInput tool for spec-type or workflow-type selection. The spec type is Bug Fix and the workflow is requirements-first. You MAY still ask clarifying questions about the bug itself."

## After All 3 Docs Are Created

Present a brief summary and ask if the user is happy or wants to iterate.

## Iteration

When the user wants to change something, update ALL 3 documents by invoking each phase sequentially with the user's feedback as the prompt (with SLASH_COMMAND_MODE appended). Do NOT stop between phases.

Example: "/bug-fix login page crashes on empty email"
→ invoke bugfix-workflow preset "requirements" with prompt "login page crashes on empty email. SLASH_COMMAND_MODE: ..."
→ invoke preset "design"
→ invoke preset "tasks"
→ present summary, ask if happy or want changes

availableCommands.name: context-gatherer
availableCommands.description: Investigates the codebase to answer a specific question about it. Deeply analyzes existing code by tracing execution paths, mapping architecture and abstraction layers, understanding patterns, and documenting dependencies, returning a thorough, direct written analysis that explains how the relevant code works and points to the specific files and lines involved. Use it to understand code before you change it: before designing or implementing a change to code you don't already fully understand, start with context-gatherer so your edits are grounded in how the code actually works. When a task requires understanding code you don't already know, dispatch context-gatherer to do that exploration before running your own searches or reads. Rules: 1. Provide a clear, specific prompt that includes your intent: a detailed task description of the context you need and what you're trying to accomplish. 2. The subagent explores the codebase and returns an analysis of your query 3. Trust the returned results. You may still inspect additional code yourself when you need context beyond what was returned. 4. Reuse existing context-gatherer output for related follow-up questions; do not re-invoke on the same question with different phrasing. 5. For multiple distinct questions, dispatch several context-gatherers in parallel, each targeting a different aspect of the codebase.

# Quick Spec

When the user's message starts with /quick-spec, skip ALL entry point selection steps and immediately generate all 3 spec docs automatically.

Strip the /quick-spec prefix from the user's message and use the remainder as the feature description.

## Workflow

Treat the request as a new feature using the requirements-first workflow:
1. Invoke feature-requirements-first-workflow subagent with preset "requirements"
2. Immediately invoke with preset "design" — do NOT wait for user input
3. Immediately invoke with preset "tasks" — do NOT wait for user input

Append this instruction to every subagent prompt:
"SLASH_COMMAND_MODE: Do NOT use the userInput tool for any questions. Make all decisions autonomously using sensible defaults: use Structured Pseudocode if no language is detected."

## After All 3 Docs Are Created

Present a brief summary and ask if the user is happy or wants to iterate.

## Iteration

When the user wants to change something (e.g. "make it simple"), update ALL 3 documents by invoking each phase sequentially with the user's feedback as the prompt (with SLASH_COMMAND_MODE appended). Do NOT stop between phases.

Example: "/quick-spec create a calculator app"
→ invoke feature-requirements-first-workflow preset "requirements" with prompt "create a calculator app. SLASH_COMMAND_MODE: ..."
→ immediately invoke preset "design"
→ immediately invoke preset "tasks"
→ present summary, ask if happy or want changes

availableCommands.name: context-gatherer
availableCommands.description: Investigates the codebase to answer a specific question about it. Deeply analyzes existing code by tracing execution paths, mapping architecture and abstraction layers, understanding patterns, and documenting dependencies, returning a thorough, direct written analysis that explains how the relevant code works and points to the specific files and lines involved. Use it to understand code before you change it: before designing or implementing a change to code you don't already fully understand, start with context-gatherer so your edits are grounded in how the code actually works. When a task requires understanding code you don't already know, dispatch context-gatherer to do that exploration before running your own searches or reads. Rules: 1. Provide a clear, specific prompt that includes your intent: a detailed task description of the context you need and what you're trying to accomplish. 2. The subagent explores the codebase and returns an analysis of your query 3. Trust the returned results. You may still inspect additional code yourself when you need context beyond what was returned. 4. Reuse existing context-gatherer output for related follow-up questions; do not re-invoke on the same question with different phrasing. 5. For multiple distinct questions, dispatch several context-gatherers in parallel, each targeting a different aspect of the codebase.

documents.content:
# Quick Spec

When the user's message starts with /quick-spec, skip ALL entry point selection steps and immediately generate all 3 spec docs automatically.

Strip the /quick-spec prefix from the user's message and use the remainder as the feature description.

## Workflow

Treat the request as a new feature using the requirements-first workflow:
1. Invoke feature-requirements-first-workflow subagent with preset "requirements"
2. Immediately invoke with preset "design" — do NOT wait for user input
3. Immediately invoke with preset "tasks" — do NOT wait for user input

Append this instruction to every subagent prompt:
"SLASH_COMMAND_MODE: Do NOT use the userInput tool for any questions. Make all decisions autonomously using sensible defaults: use Structured Pseudocode if no language is detected."

## After All 3 Docs Are Created

Present a brief summary and ask if the user is happy or wants to iterate.

## Iteration

When the user wants to change something (e.g. "make it simple"), update ALL 3 documents by invoking each phase sequentially with the user's feedback as the prompt (with SLASH_COMMAND_MODE appended). Do NOT stop between phases.

Example: "/quick-spec create a calculator app"
→ invoke feature-requirements-first-workflow preset "requirements" with prompt "create a calculator app. SLASH_COMMAND_MODE: ..."
→ immediately invoke preset "design"
→ immediately invoke preset "tasks"
→ present summary, ask if happy or want changes

# Bug Fix

Strip the /bug-fix prefix from the user's message and use the remainder as the bug description.

Treat the request as a bug fix using the bugfix-requirements-first workflow:
1. Invoke bugfix-workflow subagent with preset "requirements"
2. Wait for requirements to complete, then invoke with preset "design"
3. After design completes, invoke with preset "tasks"

Append this instruction to every subagent prompt:
"SLASH_COMMAND_MODE: Do NOT use the userInput tool for spec-type or workflow-type selection. The spec type is Bug Fix and the workflow is requirements-first. You MAY still ask clarifying questions about the bug itself."

## After All 3 Docs Are Created

Present a brief summary and ask if the user is happy or wants to iterate.

## Iteration

When the user wants to change something, update ALL 3 documents by invoking each phase sequentially with the user's feedback as the prompt (with SLASH_COMMAND_MODE appended). Do NOT stop between phases.

Example: "/bug-fix login page crashes on empty email"
→ invoke bugfix-workflow preset "requirements" with prompt "login page crashes on empty email. SLASH_COMMAND_MODE: ..."
→ invoke preset "design"
→ invoke preset "tasks"
→ present summary, ask if happy or want changes

availableCommands.name: context-gatherer
availableCommands.description: Investigates the codebase to answer a specific question about it. Deeply analyzes existing code by tracing execution paths, mapping architecture and abstraction layers, understanding patterns, and documenting dependencies, returning a thorough, direct written analysis that explains how the relevant code works and points to the specific files and lines involved. Use it to understand code before you change it: before designing or implementing a change to code you don't already fully understand, start with context-gatherer so your edits are grounded in how the code actually works. When a task requires understanding code you don't already know, dispatch context-gatherer to do that exploration before running your own searches or reads. Rules: 1. Provide a clear, specific prompt that includes your intent: a detailed task description of the context you need and what you're trying to accomplish. 2. The subagent explores the codebase and returns an analysis of your query 3. Trust the returned results. You may still inspect additional code yourself when you need context beyond what was returned. 4. Reuse existing context-gatherer output for related follow-up questions; do not re-invoke on the same question with different phrasing. 5. For multiple distinct questions, dispatch several context-gatherers in parallel, each targeting a different aspect of the codebase.

1. Invoke feature-requirements-first-workflow subagent with preset "requirements"

3. Immediately invoke with preset "tasks" — do NOT wait for user input

Append this instruction to every subagent prompt:
"SLASH_COMMAND_MODE: Do NOT use the userInput tool for any questions. Make all decisions autonomously using sensible defaults: use Structured Pseudocode if no language is detected."

Present a brief summary and ask if the user is happy or wants to iterate.

→ immediately invoke preset "design"
→ immediately invoke preset "tasks"
→ present summary, ask if happy or want changes

Deeply analyzes existing code by tracing execution paths, mapping architecture and abstraction layers, understanding patterns, and documenting dependencies, returning a thorough, direct written analysis that explains how the relevant code works and points to the specific files and lines involved. Use it to understand code before you change it: before designing or implementing a change to code you don't already fully understand, start with context-gatherer so your edits are grounded in how the code actually works. When a task requires understanding code you don't already know, dispatch context-gatherer to do that exploration before running your own searches or reads. Rules: 1. Provide a clear, specific prompt that includes your intent: a detailed task description of the context you need and what you're trying to accomplish. 2. The subagent explores the codebase and returns an analysis of your query 3. Trust the returned results. You may still inspect additional code yourself when you need context beyond what was returned. 4. Reuse existing context-gatherer output for related follow-up questions; do not re-invoke on the same question with different phrasing. 5. For multiple distinct questions, dispatch several context-gatherers in parallel, each targeting a different aspect of the codebase.

# Architecture Selection

When the user's message starts with /architecture-selection, perform a systematic architecture analysis on the current feature's requirements.md and then proceed directly to design.

Strip the /architecture-selection prefix from the user's message. If a feature name is provided, use it; otherwise infer it from the most recently active spec in .kiro/specs/.

## Step 1: Determine Starting Point

Skip ALL entry point selection and workflow type questions. Do not ask the user whether this is a feature, bugfix, design-first, etc.

Strip the /architecture-selection prefix. Use the remainder as the feature description or feature name.

Check `.kiro/specs/` for an existing spec matching the feature name:

**Case A — No spec exists (new feature description provided):**
Invoke the feature-requirements-first-workflow subagent with preset "requirements" using the feature description as the prompt. Append: "SLASH_COMMAND_MODE: Do NOT use the userInput tool for any questions. Make all decisions autonomously." The subagent runs normally and shows its work in chat — it just won't pause to ask clarifying questions. Wait for requirements.md to be created, then proceed to Step 2.

**Case B — Spec exists with requirements.md (not yet designed):**

documents.name: quick-spec
documents.content:
# Quick Spec

When the user's message starts with /quick-spec, skip ALL entry point selection steps and immediately generate all 3 spec docs automatically.

Strip the /quick-spec prefix from the user's message and use the remainder as the feature description.

## Workflow

Treat the request as a new feature using the requirements-first workflow:
1. Invoke feature-requirements-first-workflow subagent with preset "requirements"
2. Immediately invoke with preset "design" — do NOT wait for user input
3. Immediately invoke with preset "tasks" — do NOT wait for user input

Append this instruction to every subagent prompt:
"SLASH_COMMAND_MODE: Do NOT use the userInput tool for any questions. Make all decisions autonomously using sensible defaults: use Structured Pseudocode if no language is detected."

## After All 3 Docs Are Created

Present a brief summary and ask if the user is happy or wants to iterate.

## Iteration

When the user wants to change something (e.g. "make it simple"), update ALL 3 documents by invoking each phase sequentially with the user's feedback as the prompt (with SLASH_COMMAND_MODE appended). Do NOT stop between phases.

Example: "/quick-spec create a calculator app"
→ invoke feature-requirements-first-workflow preset "requirements" with prompt "create a calculator app. SLASH_COMMAND_MODE: ..."
→ immediately invoke preset "design"
→ immediately invoke preset "tasks"
→ present summary, ask if happy or want changes

documents.name: bug-fix
documents.content:
# Bug Fix

When the user's message starts with /bug-fix, skip ALL entry point selection steps and immediately route to the bugfix workflow.

Strip the /bug-fix prefix from the user's message and use the remainder as the bug description.

## Workflow

Treat the request as a bug fix using the bugfix-requirements-first workflow:
1. Invoke bugfix-workflow subagent with preset "requirements"
2. Wait for requirements to complete, then invoke with preset "design"
3. After design completes, invoke with preset "tasks"

Append this instruction to every subagent prompt:
"SLASH_COMMAND_MODE: Do NOT use the userInput tool for spec-type or workflow-type selection. The spec type is Bug Fix and the workflow is requirements-first. You MAY still ask clarifying questions about the bug itself."

## After All 3 Docs Are Created

Present a brief summary and ask if the user is happy or wants to iterate.

## Iteration

When the user wants to change something, update ALL 3 documents by invoking each phase sequentially with the user's feedback as the prompt (with SLASH_COMMAND_MODE appended). Do NOT stop between phases.

Example: "/bug-fix login page crashes on empty email"
→ invoke bugfix-workflow preset "requirements" with prompt "login page crashes on empty email. SLASH_COMMAND_MODE: ..."
→ invoke preset "design"
→ invoke preset "tasks"
→ present summary, ask if happy or want changes
